extractedText: Toronto’s Green P is going greener—and this time, it’s not just a tagline. As electric vehicle adoption continues to surge across the city, the Toronto Parking Authority is marking Earth Week with a move that feels both timely and strategic: free EV charging at more than 500 stations across Toronto. But beyond the headline-grabbing perk, the bigger story is how quickly the city’s EV infrastructure is evolving. With nearly 80% of Torontonians now living within five kilometres of a Green P charger, plugging in is no longer something reserved for early adopters—it’s becoming part of everyday city life. A city within reach For years, one of the biggest barriers to EV adoption wasn’t interest—it was access. Where do you charge if you don’t have a driveway? What if your condo doesn’t support it yet? ADVERTISEMENT That gap is closing fast. Green P’s network has now surpassed 500 charging stations across Toronto and the GTA, spanning both on-street and off-street locations. That means whether you’re running errands, heading to dinner, or parking downtown for the afternoon, chances are you’re already closer to a charger than you think. And that “80% within 5 km” stat isn’t just impressive—it’s a shift in mindset. EV charging is no longer a destination. It’s becoming part of the rhythm of the city. Photo: Courtesy From convenience to conversion Free charging for Earth Week—running from April 20 to April 24—isn’t just a feel-good initiative. It’s a smart way to get more drivers to actually try the network. ADVERTISEMENT For EV owners, it’s a bonus. For EV-curious drivers, it’s a low-risk entry point. Charging will be available at all Green P Level 2 and Level 3 stations during the promotion, accessible through apps like FLO and ChargePoint, by credit card, or RFID card. The only caveat? Standard parking fees still apply where required. It’s a small detail, but an important one—it reinforces that this isn’t a pilot or a pop-up. It’s a fully functioning system, just temporarily free to use. What’s powering the growth Toronto’s EV adoption has surged by 380% over the past six years, and infrastructure is finally catching up. Green P’s expansion is being built in collaboration with partners like Toronto Hydro, FLO, and ChargePoint, with a clear goal: make Toronto one of the most EV-accessible cities in Canada. ADVERTISEMENT What’s coming next: Ultrafast Level 3 chargers (100kW) launching in 2026, starting at Carpark 43 10 new on-street Level 2 chargers rolling out by the end of Q2 2026 Hundreds more chargers planned over the next two years EV integration into the Green P app, used by over 3 million drivers It all aligns with the City of Toronto’s TransformTO Net Zero Strategy, which targets 30% EV adoption by 2030—a number that feels increasingly realistic as infrastructure scales. More than a moment—it’s a shift What makes this initiative interesting isn’t just the free charging—it’s what it represents. ADVERTISEMENT We’re at a point where the conversation around EVs is shifting from “should I?” to “why not?” Between federal incentives offering up to $5,000 per vehicle and a growing, citywide charging network, the friction points are starting to disappear. And when accessibility meets affordability—even temporarily—you start to see real behaviour change. Earth Week just happens to be the catalyst. ADVERTISEMENT What to expect during free EV charging week If you’re planning to plug in, here’s what you need to know: Dates: April 20 (12:00 a.m.) to April 24 (11:59 p.m.) Where: All 500+ Green P EV charging stations across Toronto Cost: Charging is free; parking fees may still apply How to access: Via FLO or ChargePoint apps, credit card, or RFID Whether you’re a daily EV driver or just curious to see how it works, this is one of the easiest entry points the city has offered to date. Plugging into what’s next Toronto isn’t just preparing for an electric future—it’s already building it, one charger at a time. ADVERTISEMENT And for one week this April, the barrier to trying it disappears entirely. So if you’ve been on the fence, consider this your sign. Plug in, Toronto.
